text:
maria_sales: FYI Acme (Alice/CTO) wants an air-gapped POC on their on-prem k8s. They specifically asked about packaging (delta vs full), upgrade cadence, and any pricing/one-time fees.

alice_cto: Hi — important: no egress, strict change window (monthly patch window), limited bandwidth to pull artifacts. Looking for a lightweight installer we can review. Also need rollback plan.

devon_se: Understood. We offer signed bundles + chunked delta updates for customers with limited bandwidth. Two delivery modes for POC: full bundle sideload (sneakernet/USB) or signed deltas via an allowed jumpbox.

rahul_ops: Technical constraints: our operator supports k8s 1.22+. For air-gap we generate an offline bundle containing: container images tarball, operator manifests, model artifacts (quantized, if requested), SBOM, and a signatures.tar (signed by our CI). Upgrade cadence can be configured per-customer, but our recommended cadence for seeded POCs is monthly security patch + quarterly feature rollouts.

alice_cto: Can you confirm bundle sizes? Their infra team will only accept <=10GB per transfer for initial onboarding.

devon_se: Typical full bundle w/ base model (7B quantized) ~4-6GB. Delta patches are usually under 200-500MB depending on model deltas and metadata. We can provide a minimized bundle (no dev tools) for POC.

tess_security: Quick security notes: we sign bundles with our root signing key (we can do a customer-provided key via HSM for Private deployments). We include SBOM and reproducible checksums. For compliance, we can produce a short attestation doc for the artifact chain. Also need to confirm TLS termination and internal cert rotation plan. @maria_sales please ping legal for any additional export control requirements.

alice_cto: HSM integration is a requirement for production; POC can use our jumpbox for verification. Also, how do licensing and pricing work offline? Any one-time packaging fee?

maria_sales: Pricing: base hosted-per-token doesn't apply here. For Private/offline we have a platform license + optional reserved capacity. For POC we typically charge a modest one-time airgap packaging + signing fee (covers SBOM/attestation + custom packaging) — I can draft an estimate.

devon_se: Operationally, upgrade process for the customer: 1) they place bundle on jumpbox or USB, 2) run `operatorctl apply-offline --bundle signed-bundle.tar.gz`, 3) operator verifies signature + SBOM, 4) rolling upgrade across replica sets. Rollback supported via operator snapshot which we keep in-cluster (pre-upgrade). We'll document commands in the runbook.

rahul_ops: Two caveats: a) If they enforce immutable infra (no outbound) we need their cluster to approve our CA for signature verification or provide their verification keys. b) Large model swaps (e.g., 7B -> 13B) may require node capacity changes — that’s outside automatic delta.

alice_cto: They also asked about telemetry — must be opt-out and no telemetry leaves the network.

tess_security: We support full telemetry opt-out for air-gapped deployments. We provide offline logs and an admin diagnostics bundle that can be shared via secure channels if they want support help.

devon_se: For POC timeline: can produce sample signed bundle + runbook in ~3 business days, full minimized bundle in 7 days. Need final model choice and whether they want quantized artifacts.

maria_sales: Action items: (1) Alice — confirm model size (7B quantized OK?) and preferred delivery method (USB vs jumpbox). (2) Devon — prepare sample signed bundle + runbook (3 days). (3) Tess — prepare attestation template and telemetry opt-out language. (4) Rahul — confirm operator compatibility matrix and rollback steps in docs.

alice_cto: Confirmed: start with 7B quantized, jumpbox approach preferred, monthly patch window ok. We'll share legal contact for licensing.

deploy-bot: Artifact uploaded: `signed-bundle-sample-4991237890.tar.gz` (sha256: abc123...); runbook draft: `airgap-runbook-4991237890.md`

maria_sales: Great — I'll get the one-time packaging estimate to Acme today and loop in legal. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
